books.title: Leaves of Grass
books.author: Walt Whitman
books.desc: Whitman's lifelong book of free verse, celebrating the self, the body, nature and American democracy, from "Song of Myself" to his last poems.
about: Leaves of Grass gathers hundreds of poems written over almost forty years, including "Song of Myself", "I Sing the Body Electric", "Crossing Brooklyn Ferry", "Out of the Cradle Endlessly Rocking" and "Song of the Open Road". In long, unrhymed lines, the poet speaks for himself and for everyone, cataloguing the people, landscapes, cities and work of America, the experiences of the body and the soul, and the Civil War and its dead.

Whitman's poems, which rarely rhyme or follow conventional metre, celebrate nature, the individual and democracy. Their frank delight in the body and sensual pleasure made the book highly controversial in its time; it has since become one of the central works of American poetry.

Whitman self-published the first edition, a slim volume of twelve poems, in 1855, and spent the rest of his life revising and expanding the book until his death in 1892; the last edition contained more than 400 poems.
books.author_short: American poet, essayist and journalist (1819–1892), author of Leaves of Grass.
author_long: Walt Whitman was born on 31 May 1819 in Huntington, on Long Island, and lived in Brooklyn as a child and through much of his career, and worked as a journalist. During the American Civil War he went to Washington and worked in hospitals caring for the wounded. After a stroke he moved to Camden, New Jersey, where he died on 26 March 1892.
He devoted his life to Leaves of Grass, first published in 1855 and continually revised and expanded. He also wrote essays and two novels.

books.title: The Home and the World
books.author: Rabindranath Tagore
books.desc: In Bengal during the Swadeshi movement, a sheltered wife is drawn between her gentle husband and a fiery nationalist leader.
about: Bimala, the wife of the wealthy and liberal landowner Nikhil, has lived in the seclusion of the women's quarters until her husband encourages her to step into the outside world. There she meets his friend Sandip, a charismatic leader of the Swadeshi movement, which calls for the boycott of British goods. Swept up by his passion and his words, Bimala becomes devoted to the cause and to Sandip, while the young Amulya is ready to sacrifice everything for him. The story is told in turn by Bimala, Nikhil and Sandip.

Tagore's novel contrasts Nikhil, rational and opposed to violence, with Sandip, who will let nothing stand in his way, and examines nationalism, the place of women, and the conflict between the home and the world outside.

Ghare Baire was published in Bengali in 1916. It is set against the Swadeshi movement that followed the Partition of Bengal in 1905. The English translation by the author's nephew, Surendranath Tagore, made with input from the author, was published in 1919.
books.author_short: Bengali poet, novelist, playwright and composer (1861–1941), the first non-European winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature.
author_long: Rabindranath Tagore was born on 7 May 1861 in the Jorasanko mansion in Calcutta, the youngest of thirteen surviving children of Debendranath Tagore. He wrote poetry from the age of eight and became one of the foremost figures of the Bengal Renaissance. He died on 7 August 1941.
In 1913 he became the first non-European to win a Nobel Prize in Literature, for the poetry of Gitanjali. His best-known works include Gitanjali, the novel Gora and The Home and the World.

books.title: The Voyage Out
books.author: Virginia Woolf
books.desc: A sheltered young Englishwoman sails to South America on her father's ship and begins to discover the world, ideas and love.
about: Rachel Vinrace, a shy young woman of twenty-four brought up by her aunts in Richmond, sails for South America on her father's ship, the Euphrosyne, with her aunt Helen Ambrose and her uncle Ridley. Among the passengers for part of the voyage are Richard and Clarissa Dalloway. At the hotel in the resort of Santa Marina, Rachel meets a group of English tourists, among them the intellectual St. John Hirst and the aspiring novelist Terence Hewet, with whom she falls in love.

Woolf's first novel follows a young woman's journey from a cloistered life to freedom and self-discovery, with sharp observation of English society abroad. It introduces Clarissa Dalloway, the central character of Woolf's later Mrs Dalloway.
The Voyage Out was published in 1915 by Duckworth. Woolf began it around 1910, perhaps as early as 1907, and revised it extensively during a difficult period of her life.

books.title: Childhood
books.author: Leo Tolstoy
books.desc: A boy's memories of his tenth year on a Russian country estate: his tutor, his family, his first friendships and the death of his mother.
about: On the morning of 12 August, three days after his tenth birthday, Nikolenka is woken by his German tutor, Karl Ivanitch. He recalls the days that follow on the family estate and in Moscow: lessons and games with his brother Woloda, hunting with his father, the holy fool Grisha, the devoted housekeeper Natalia Savishna, a children's dance party, his admiration for the handsome Seriosha Iwin and his first feelings of love, until the illness and death of his mother.
Tolstoy's first published work explores the inner life of a sensitive boy with great psychological precision, and evokes the joys, fears, shame and tenderness of childhood.

Childhood appeared in the November 1852 issue of the journal The Contemporary, signed only with Tolstoy's initials. It is the first of a trilogy, followed by Boyhood and Youth. This English translation is by C. J. Hogarth.

books.title: Pan
books.author: Knut Hamsun
books.desc: A solitary hunter living in a forest hut in northern Norway recalls a summer of passionate, tormented love for a merchant's daughter.
about: Lieutenant Thomas Glahn, a former officer and hunter, writes down his memories of a summer two years earlier, when he lived alone in a hut in the forests of Nordland with his dog Aesop. He meets Edvarda, the proud and capricious daughter of the merchant Mack, and the two are strongly drawn to each other, yet neither understands the other's love. As Edvarda torments him and other suitors appear, Glahn finds comfort with the gentle Eva, and his impulsive behaviour drives him further apart from the people of the town.

Hamsun's lyrical novel describes the intense northern summer, the forest and the sea, and the shifting moods of a man close to nature and estranged from society. It ends with an epilogue about Glahn's death.
Pan was published in 1894. This English translation is by W. W. Worster, with an introduction by Edwin Björkman.
